chapter: Touring abroad and the future of music
title: University support for jazz departments versus football
summary: Music departments are poorly supported and can never compete with football and basketball, but progress in the last 15-20 years has been phenomenal.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: I see, okay. A lot of these departments that we're talking about, that we know of, are not too well supported by the administrations of the universities. That is true in many, many places.
I don't think we'll ever be able to compete with football and basketball.
But we know that in front, so we don't go there with that intent.
But there are a lot of band directors who are just doing it beyond their call of duty, of course.
That's right, and for this they should win a lot of points.
Yeah, I think there should be more subsidy by various -- government or whatever.
But I stated the case when I said we'll never be able to really compete with basketball and football, because they have a big income, which is part of the whole
And we're just a small part of that. We're the background to the game.
And we have to be realistic and face that. But also, I think the strides that have been made in the last 15 to 20 years are phenomenal, and I think we can do nothing but keep winning.
